clue.text: Decorate man diving into stream …

indicators.note: something that dives into a stream ends up inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a beck is a northern English word for a small stream
Ed is a man's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: Someone adorns a swimmer as he plunges into a brook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diving into' is the insertion signal. The dots joining this clue to the next are only for show: each clue is solved on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to adorn something with ornaments or finery is to deck it out.

clue.text: Dicky sort of driver

definitions.meaning: a dicky is an old British term for a folding extra seat at the rear of a car
a passenger who nags from behind with unwanted advice is called this kind of driver

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the rear place in a car, and the phrase describing an interfering passenger.

clue.text: Hollow? Had some food, being equipped to chew it

parts.note: a dent is a hollow in a surface
ate is the past tense of eat

explanation.surface: Someone feeling empty has a meal, having what it takes to bite it.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful description: the adjective means having teeth, the equipment for chewing.

clue.text: Vehicle over the hill, but it fills the breach, we hear

definitions.text: it fills the breach, we hear

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece stands above the second

parts.note: a cart is a simple wheeled vehicle
a ridge is a long narrow hilltop

explanation.surface: A truck past its best still plugs the gap in the line, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' stacks the pieces in a down entry. 'we hear' belongs to the definition: the breach sounds like the breech, the back of a gun where a round is loaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Punning description: a round of ammunition goes into a gun's breech, which is said the same as breach.

clue.text: … in bid to destroy criminal

indicators.note: one piece sits within the letters of the other, as the word plainly says

parts.note: a bid at an auction is an offer
to end something is to finish it off, to destroy it

explanation.surface: Someone joins an auction hoping to ruin a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion signal is the plain 'in' after the dots. 'criminal' looks like an adjective or an anagram signal but is the noun defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a noun: a lawbreaker is one who commits an offence.

clue.text: Rubs gently, fits fallen arch support

indicators.note: something fallen has tumbled down in a heap, so the letters lie in disorder

explanation.surface: A soft massage, then an insole is fitted for a flat foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fallen' rearranges RUBS GENTLY FITS. The surface suggests feet and fallen arches, but the support is architectural.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a slanting stone prop, itself a half arch, that holds up a cathedral wall.

clue.text: Heron, for example, starts to relish eating trout

parts.note: eg is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: the start of each word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A wading bird begins to enjoy its fish supper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for example' looks as if it qualifies the heron but supplies letters; 'starts to' takes the first letter of each following word.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a white long-legged wading bird of the heron family.

clue.text: Carrying round battle-axe to coerce

indicators.note: what is carried is held within, so one piece has the other inside it

parts.note: a battle-axe is a fierce, domineering woman, also called a dragon
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone lugs a circular medieval weapon about to force others to obey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrying' places O inside DRAGON. The battle-axe is a formidable woman, not a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to force someone into doing something.

clue.text: New version of film about cause

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to make something happen is to cause it

explanation.surface: A fresh cut of a documentary about a campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a movie shot again with a new cast is one of these.

clue.text: Bother! Both taps fluctuate

parts.note: blow is a mild exclamation of annoyance, like bother
a basin's two taps are the hot and the cold

explanation.surface: An annoyed cry as the two taps keep changing their flow.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to keep changing one's mind or enthusiasm, to vacillate.

clue.text: Money-gathering is at the heart of things

parts.note: a cent is a small coin, an example of money
a rally is a mass meeting or gathering

explanation.surface: Making money is said to be what really matters in life.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'Money-gathering' must be ignored: the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverbial equivalent: something placed in the middle is positioned in this way.

clue.text: Kingdom needs genuine leader of men

parts.note: genuine means real, not fake

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front

explanation.surface: A country requires a true commander for its troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a monarch's domain, the land a king or queen rules.

clue.text: Animal eats fish and fowl

indicators.note: what an animal eats goes inside it, so one piece is swallowed by the other

parts.note: a sow is a female pig, an animal
a parr is a young salmon

explanation.surface: A creature dines on both fish and poultry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eats' is the insertion signal. 'fish and fowl' reads as the menu, but only the fish is eaten; the fowl is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose example: fowl in its old broad sense means any bird, and this is a small common one.

clue.text: System needs points — with a couple, is out of danger

parts.note: north and east are two points of the compass, N and E
a couple is two

indicators.note: one word is taken out of another, leaving the rest behind

parts.note: risk is danger
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: A scheme must score, and with two more it will be safe.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface phrase 'is out of danger' must be split up: 'out of' says the word 'is' leaves a synonym of danger, and two letters remain.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an interconnected arrangement, as in a rail or computer one.

clue.text: A loaf in the van

parts.note: loaf is British slang for the head, from rhyming slang 'loaf of bread'

explanation.surface: Some bread sits in the delivery vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: The van here is the vanguard, the front of an advancing force, not a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the van is the foremost part, so being in it means being out in front.

clue.text: Moving in circles, military underlings get sarcastic

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
a biting remark is a sarcastic, cutting one

explanation.surface: Junior soldiers mingling socially start making cutting remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal description: going round and round a body, as a satellite does.

clue.text: 26 besiegers hope to

definitions.meaning: the answer at 26 across means to happen, and so does this phrase
an army besieging a town hopes to capture the stronghold

explanation.definitionFit: Two readings: the phrase means to happen, and word by word it means to capture a town.

clue.text: Person responsible for film is female priest

parts.note: Di is a woman's name, short for Diana
a rector is a parish priest in the Church of England

explanation.surface: The woman who made the movie is also a member of the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the one in charge of how a movie is made.

clue.text: Agreement made by witches with worker

parts.note: a coven is a group of witches
a worker ant is the crossword's favourite labourer

explanation.surface: Some witches strike a deal with a labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a solemn binding pact or contract.

clue.text: Reorganize force if you require a policeman

indicators.note: to reorganize is to put things into a new arrangement, here the letters that follow

explanation.surface: Restructure the constabulary whenever one more constable is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reorganize' rearranges FORCE IF. The 'force' reads as the police force, which suits the answer nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: constables are addressed by this title.

clue.text: Used by sheikh, a kind of sand-coloured cloth

indicators.note: the letters are used by the phrase that follows, forming a run within it

explanation.surface: An Arab ruler wears a fabric the colour of the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used by' marks a run of letters spanning the next words, across the comma.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the dull yellowish-brown fabric used for military uniforms.

clue.text: Within which man's got moving

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift about into a new order

explanation.surface: A crowd in the middle of which a fellow has started to stir.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a preposition: in the midst of, surrounded by.

clue.text: Last two thirds of musical are offensive

indicators.note: of a nine-letter word only the final six letters are kept

parts.note: musical as an adjective means tuneful, melodious
the first third of the word, which is dropped

explanation.surface: Most of the later part of a stage show is in poor taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last two thirds of' drops the first three letters of a nine-letter word. 'musical' is an adjective here, not a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: hateful or repellent.

clue.text: Fare badly, taken in by worthless swindle

indicators.note: something taken in is received inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a dud cheque or coin is a worthless one

indicators.note: badly done means done wrongly, so the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone does poorly after falling for a useless con.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' makes FRAU from the first word, which 'taken in by' puts inside the synonym of worthless. 'taken in' tempts as 'deceived', which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to cheat someone out of money.

clue.text: Several days acting for the stage

parts.note: Apr is short for April, a stretch of thirty days
an actor who is on is performing at that moment

explanation.surface: A performer spends a few days playing roles in the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Part for whole: the strip of a theatre platform in front of the curtain.

clue.text: Carpet salesman has to travel

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
to rove is to wander or travel about

explanation.surface: A man who sells rugs is obliged to go on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' is a verb here: in British English to carpet someone is to give them a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to scold or reprimand someone.

clue.text: Happen to turn firm with dog

indicators.note: to turn something is to face it the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a cur is a mongrel or bad-tempered dog

explanation.surface: Someone chances to become strict with a pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' sends CO backwards to give OC. 'firm' reads as an adjective in the surface but is a business.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to come about or come to pass.

clue.text: Hang louts making vicious attack

indicators.note: the letters before it are the material from which something new is made

explanation.surface: A call to string up thugs who carry out a savage assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' turns the letters of HANG LOUTS into a new word.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a fierce and violent assault.

clue.text: Instrumental piece composed to introduce Anton Dvorak originally

indicators.note: to introduce something is to bring it in, so one piece takes the other inside

parts.note: a composed person is calm and serene

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A work without singers was written to present the composer Dvorak to the public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' picks the composer's initials and 'to introduce' is the insertion signal. 'composed' reads as 'written' but means calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a light work for a small ensemble, like those Dvorak wrote for strings and for winds.

clue.text: Improve on punter

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to surpass or do more than a previous effort
a punter is British slang for a gambler, one who places a wager

explanation.surface: Someone tries to do more than a gambler manages.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a verb meaning to surpass, and a noun for someone who gambles.
